subject: Phased capacity increase — options for pricing, credits, and co-term
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <contracts@brightpoint.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity increase and pricing path — mid-contract uplift

Hi Marissa,

We are seeing a steady rise in inference usage across two product lines and expect an additional ~30% token consumption over the next 90 days. Procurement asked me to reach out for options that provide predictable unit pricing during the ramp and a clean path to co-term with our existing annual agreement.

Attached is our last three months of usage (Brightpoint_Monthly_Usage.csv). Key asks from our side:
- A soft cap/buffer we can burst into without immediate penalty
- A way to carry unused top-up capacity forward if we overprovision during early months
- Co-term alignment with our Dec 31 renewal date (we’d prefer not to extend the contract length)

What packaging or temporary credit models do you typically suggest for this? We have a procurement review next Thursday and would like a written option set to share.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Contracts Manager, Brightpoint Analytics
attachments: Brightpoint_Monthly_Usage.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <contracts@brightpoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity increase and pricing path — mid-contract uplift

Hi Samantha,

Thanks for the data — that helps. I sketched a pragmatic two-part option you can present to procurement quickly. High level: keep your annual co-term, add a phased top-up with an early ramp discount and an unused-capacity credit bucket. Details below. I attached a short one-pager (Marissa_Proposal_PhasedScaling_v1.pdf).

Option A — Phased Scaling + Credit Exchange (recommended)
- Baseline uplift: +30% of current committed units for an initial 90-day window.
- Discounting: 15% off list for month 1, 10% for month 2, 5% for month 3 (applied to uplift units only).
- Credit bucket: 10% of the uplifted spend converted into a carry-forward credit pool if not consumed within the 90-day window; credits apply only to inference units in next billing period(s) through co-term.
- Bursting: soft-burst allowed up to 15% above uplift at on-demand list pricing; anything above will be assessed the next billing cycle (we can give 48-hour notice window).
- Legal/ops: this is an amendment, no baseline term extension — co-term remains Dec 31, 2026.

Option B — Fixed Monthly Top-up (simpler)
- Fixed monthly top-up quantity purchased for the remainder of term; no step discounts but predictable MRC. Credits are not issued for unused top-ups.

Operational notes / next steps
- If you like Option A we’ll prepare an amendment + a short SOW for the ramp mechanics. Ben, can you validate the estimated MRC delta and confirm the credit accounting approach? Sofia, please run this by finance for invoicing cadence and whether we need an escrowed voucher for the credit pool.

Samantha — if procurement needs a tighter discount cadence (e.g., front-loading more of the discount into month 1), mention that in your reply and we’ll iterate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa,

Quick sanity check on the numbers for Option A:
- Estimated incremental MRC (30% uplift on current run-rate): ~$12,000/month (ballpark, dependent on token mix).
- Effective uplift unit price post-discounts (blended across 3 months): ~ $0.045 per 1k-token equivalent.
- Credit pool: create a tracked credit line equal to 10% of the uplift spend; credits will be journaled and applied at invoice generation toward usage tokens.

Sofia — please confirm whether we require an internal finance approval for the 15% front-loaded discount or if the AE team can approve up to 10% without escalations. If procurement insists on 15% for month 1, we'll need an approval ticket and a short justification (volume growth and retention).

If legal is comfortable with an amendment that only updates committed units and billing rules (no term change), we can push a draft amendment and SOW to Samantha by EOD Thursday.

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear Option A details. Procurement reviewed and we have two asks before we can sign off:
1) Can you move more of the discount into the first 60 days? Our forecast shows most of the burst will be front-loaded; a 15% discount for month 1 and 12% for month 2 would materially help our unit economics.
2) We prefer the carry-forward credit pool but need visibility into how credits appear on invoices and that they can offset overages across product lines under the same account.

Attached is a draft SOW showing the expected monthly usage profile for July–Dec; procurement wants to circulate a clean amendment + SOW to legal. If you can provide a DocuSign-ready amendment and SOW by Friday we can route for signatures the following week.

Also attaching SOW_draft.docx for your reference.

Samantha Lee
Contracts Manager, Brightpoint Analytics
